Make each defect a defined repair.

We repair the everyday building defects that interrupt an otherwise busy property. A single damaged door and a list across several tenancies need different preparation. We identify each location, check the surrounding construction and agree the repair and finish before organising attendance.

01 / Doors and hardware

A door works as an assembly.

We inspect the door leaf, hinges, frame, strike and closer as an assembly. Where a door rubs or fails to latch, we check movement through the closing arc and look for looseness or damage at the fixings before agreeing a repair.

  • What we check

    We record where the door catches, whether the latch meets the strike and whether the hinges or frame move under use. That tells us which parts of the opening need attention.

  • What a local repair covers

    When the frame and fixing points are sound, we can plan an adjustment, local refixing or replacement of a compatible part. We check operation after refitting before confirming completion.

  • What we scope separately

    A distorted frame, damaged backing, unmatched hardware or work affecting a fire or smoke door requires its own scope and an agreed check before returning the opening to use.

  • A seaside door that rubs or will not latch

    We inspect the leaf and frame gaps, hinge play, closer operation and latch engagement together. Deposits on a sound finish can be a maintenance item. If the closer is loose or the latch is out of line, we check the fixing points and geometry before deciding on adjustment or compatible parts. A distorted frame or failed substrate changes the repair boundary. We record the opening number and the closing and latching checks after repair.

02 / Walls and ceilings

Read the surface before refinishing.

We quote against hardware, boards, finish matching, special orders and access to backing before scheduling repair.

Check door clearance, the strike and the frame together. For wall damage, distinguish marks, broken edges and loose backing before specifying the finish.

Door action and wall finishes should be recorded separately even when the two defects are in the same room. For a dragging door, we note where it catches and whether it still latches. For repeated bubbling on adjoining walls, we identify the wet boundary and decide which finish can safely be retained.

  • A wall or ceiling is damaged

    We establish the affected area, board or surface condition and what must be removed. A water-stained ceiling also needs its moisture source addressed before the final finish is reinstated.

  • Joinery or fittings are loose

    We inspect the fixing points, supporting material and matching parts. The scope distinguishes adjusting or securing an item from replacing damaged components.

  • Boards, timber and substrate

    We confirm the existing build-up and sound fixing areas before choosing replacement material. Repair dimensions and adjacent damage determine how far the work extends.

  • Colour, sheen and hardware

    We use available product details and site samples to discuss matching. The quote identifies where a local finish is suitable and where a larger visible surface needs attention.

  • Bubbling paint, stained ceilings and swollen joinery

    We compare where rain hits the envelope, which pipes or equipment run overhead and when the stain changes. A photo helps locate the affected finish, but staining alone does not establish the source or the depth of damage. Once the moisture source is addressed, we check whether the backing and fixings are sound enough for a patch. Soft board or swollen joinery may need replacement before matching the finish. Drying, dust protection and coating conditions can mean a separate return visit.

From protection to a working finish

A dragging door and a damaged wall beside it can share a work area without sharing a cause. Keep the door’s closing check separate from the wall repair and agree when the route can reopen after each.

  1. 01

    Mark and protect

    We confirm the agreed item list and protect adjacent floors, furniture and finishes before opening or removing affected material.

  2. 02

    Repair and reinstate

    We address the fixing or substrate, install the agreed parts, and complete the specified patching and finishing stages.

  3. 03

    Check and clear

    We check door operation or the repaired surface, clear the agreed work area and record any remaining item requiring separate approval.

Work around the people using the space

The work plan records keys, access, noise, dust, shared routes, surface drying before furniture returns and return visits.

What shapes the quotation

  • Quantity and condition

    The number of locations, repair area, height, substrate condition and matching materials define the labour and material allowance.

  • Access and finish stages

    We itemise agreed protection, access equipment, waste and return visits, so a small repair is not confused with a complete room refurbishment.

Record by opening or room.

We check operation and the finish against the original defect list. Where a stain or loose fixing points to a separate cause, we record what must be resolved before finishing.

A clear record against your list

We identify completed items by room, location or defect number. The handover records the agreed finish and operation checks, available completion photos and any parts or separate works still outstanding.

  • Door or room number
  • Operation and finish checks
  • Backing and moisture checks

Common questions

Does a sticking door always need replacing?
Check alignment, hinges, fixings, latch and closer to distinguish hardware adjustment from work to a damaged leaf or frame.
Can several small jobs be quoted together?
Yes. A numbered list with locations and photos helps us confirm quantities and materials. We group practical tasks and identify anything needing separate access, parts or a later finish stage.
Can bubbling paint or a stained ceiling be repaired straight away?
We identify the moisture source and check the backing first. Sound, dry backing may take a patch. Soft board, swollen joinery or failed fixings change the repair scope and can require a separate finishing visit.
